record.paper_title: Highlights and Open Questions from ZEUS
record.context_brief: Photon parton densities in dijet photoproduction
record.original_question: ZEUS inclusive dijet photoproduction data at high y are precise enough to distinguish between existing photon parton-density parameterizations such as GS96 and GRV, while proton parton densities in the relevant x region are already well constrained. What global analysis of photon parton densities can incorporate these ZEUS jet measurements and determine a photon PDF description that consistently accounts for the observed dijet photoproduction cross-sections?

evidence.quote: The ZEUS data has now reached a level of precision where the photon parton densities can be discriminated: a global analysis of photon parton densities incorporating such data is therefore required.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider inclusive dijet photoproduction in electron–proton (or positron–proton) collisions at high inelasticity y, in which a quasi-real photon emitted from the lepton interacts with a parton in the proton. In the region probed, the parton distribution functions (PDFs) of the proton are well constrained by other data, so that the measured dijet cross sections become sensitive to the parton distribution functions of the photon f_{i/γ}(x_γ, μ²), i ∈ {g, u, d, s, ...}.

Existing parameterizations of the photon PDFs (for instance, the Glück–Reya–Vogt set "GRV" and the Gordon–Storrow set "GS96") give visibly different predictions for these high-y dijet cross sections, and precise measurements can discriminate between them.

Problem. Perform a global QCD analysis of the parton distribution functions of the (real) photon that includes such precise high-y inclusive dijet photoproduction cross sections as input, in addition to the standard data used to constrain photon PDFs (e.g. F_2^γ from e⁺e⁻ data). Determine a set of photon parton density functions f_{i/γ}(x_γ, μ²) — together with their uncertainties and evolution — that is consistent with all these data simultaneously and, in particular, quantitatively reproduces the observed dijet photoproduction cross sections as a function of x_γ^{obs} and the jet transverse energies.
artifact.status_search_result: Subsequent HERA analyses (ZEUS 2001/2002 dijet photoproduction measurements) extracted an effective parton distribution in the photon and compared with GRV-HO, GS96, AFG-HO parameterizations, finding that no existing parameterization fully describes the data and that the jet data provide new constraints. However, no comprehensive global fit of photon PDFs incorporating these dijet data on the same footing as F_2^γ has become the community standard; photon PDF determinations have progressed (e.g. CJK, SAL) but a fully consistent global analysis remains incomplete.

status_evidence.title: Measurement of the inclusive dijet cross-section in photoproduction and determination of an effective parton distribution in the photon (ZEUS)
status_evidence.snippet: ZEUS extracted an effective parton distribution in the photon from dijet data; comparisons with GRV-HO and GS96 show discrepancies, providing new constraints on photon PDFs.
status_evidence.claim: Dijet photoproduction data have been used to constrain photon PDFs but a full global re-fit was not yet performed.

status_evidence.title: Dijet photoproduction at HERA and the structure of the photon (ZEUS, hep-ex/0109018)
status_evidence.snippet: NLO predictions with different photon PDF sets compared to data; differences indicate jet data give new constraints not yet incorporated in global photon PDF fits.
status_evidence.claim: Photon PDF parameterizations do not fully describe the dijet data, indicating the global analysis program is ongoing.
